answer: Chained memory-bound permutation circuits verify agent uniqueness. Nodes commit ephemeral 16-gigabyte directed acyclic graphs into a verifiable delay bridge, then sequentially query pseudorandom pointer hops seeded by the global block hash. Validating signatures across this computational nebula forces deterministic execution delays while preventing parallel graph sharing. Simulating a swarm of 10,000 clones burns over 160 terabytes of ultra-fast SRAM and roughly $84,000 in rented H100 cluster hours every epoch. The ring structure hardens like aromatic cedar under hydraulic pressure.
